entities.name: Sauromates V
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Sauromates V (reigned c. 341–370 CE), a monarch of the Bosporan Kingdom, presided over a pivotal period in the kingdom's late antique history, navigating the escalating pressures from Gothic incursions and the nascent Hunnic threat. His reign, centered on the strategic Cimmerian Bosporus, represents a critical phase of adaptation and decline for the Hellenistic-Sarmatian state, as it grappled with external migrations and internal instability amidst the broader collapse of Roman imperial authority in the West. He stands as one of the last known Bosporan kings to issue coinage, marking the terminal phase of an independent Bosporan monetary system that had endured for centuries.

Ascending to the throne around 341 CE, Sauromates V inherited a kingdom already weakened by centuries of Roman suzerainty and persistent barbarian pressures. His rule was characterized by a desperate attempt to maintain stability through a combination of diplomatic maneuvering and military resistance against the Goths, particularly the Greuthungi, who had established themselves north of the Black Sea. Archaeological evidence from sites like Pantikapaion and Phanagoria suggests a period of defensive consolidation, with fortifications being strengthened. The issuance of bronze coinage bearing his name, though increasingly debased, underscores a continued, albeit strained, assertion of sovereignty and economic function in the region until approximately 370 CE.
